title: The Core, Separated
summary: Your round-1 red poster, ported as it was, with one change: the big 10 is now a darker, unclickable information panel, and 'Request a System Audit' is its own solid paper button beside it, so the fact and the action can no longer be confused — now with the new cut-corner button.
story: This is the decision. 'Sound like you?' answers the two fit ledgers directly above, and the statement asks once: 'Request the / System Audit.' The panel says what the audit is (ten working days, fixed scope, kickoff to readout). The note says what happens at its end, the readout (if installation makes sense we scope it there; if not, the plan is still yours). The band says what happens after the click (three questions, a 30-minute call with the founding team, Day 01) and where this sits in the method (Phase 01 / 04 · Diagnose). The footer's index comes after.
motion: Standalone demo (plays on load and is at rest by about 2.4s): the label fades in, 'Request the' rises out of its mask, and the lighter 'System Audit.' follows 320ms later. The paper rule draws at 0.8s. The lede rises at 0.9s and the two doors at 1.0s, so the button is in place before the panel arrives.

The one orchestrated moment, round 1's 'installed' beat, kept: at 1.15s the deep-red panel opens from its bottom-left corner (a 750ms clip reveal). The 10 and 'Working days · fixed scope' fade in, then the ten day-ticks along its foot ink in left to right, 40ms apart, and 'Kickoff' and 'Readout' appear. The note rises at 1.2s, and the band's hairline draws across the page with its two lines fading in.
Removed from round 1: the 00 → 10 count-up (the page's one counter belongs to the system section). Nothing loops.

Interaction: only the doors respond. The paper button warms to blush and its ↗ nudges up-right; the contact link's underline brightens and its → nudges. With the keyboard, each door shows a paper focus ring. The panel has no link, no hover state, no pointer cursor and no arrow, and the Tab key skips it.
On the live page: the same sequence plays once when the red plane scrolls into view. With reduced motion the finished state shows at once. There is no script.
addressed: 'We should just go with the round 1 version': this is round 1 A, ported as it was. It keeps the red plane, the 120px two-voice statement flush left, the short paper rule, the solid object with the big 10 at bottom-left, the lede beside it, the note at right, and the hairline band at the foot with 'Phase 01 / 04 · Diagnose'. Same sizes and spacing; the one grid change is the channel described next.

'Create a clear separation between the 10-number thing and the request system audit button': they are now two objects. The 10 sits in a panel one shade darker than the red, and the button is the only thing on the plane lighter than the red. Dark means read, paper means act. The panel has no arrow, no hover and no link. The button is the same solid paper 'Request a System Audit' used across the site. There is now also a full column of plain red between them (135px from the panel's edge to the button): the lede and the doors start one column later, so the button no longer sits against the panel's edge as if it belonged to it, and the note is set flush to the right margin so the row stays balanced.

'A combination of colors, or maybe borders, whichever looks the best': I built both and compared them. A thin paper outline around the 10 looked like a second, ghost button next to the real one. The solid deep-red panel never reads as clickable, and it keeps the solid-block feel you liked in round 1, so I kept the panel.

Not the round-3 look you called AI-generated: there is no printed document, no registration marks and no stack of small spec rows. Not round 2's 'too basic' either: the solid object is back, and its foot carries a quiet ten-tick ruler, one tick per working day, from Kickoff to Readout.

The agreed copy is in: 'Request the / System Audit.' (D5), the label 'Sound like you?', the lede 'One diagnostic maps the architecture underneath your pipeline. If it makes sense, we install it and run it with you. What we build, you keep.' (the middle sentence is positioning E6, so the last words before the button say Kelwin installs and runs the system, not only audits it) 'Deployment window open' is gone (D7). In its place is a true line from the audit page, under the label 'At the readout': 'If installation makes sense, we scope it there. If not, the plan is still yours.'
notes: FIG. numbering dropped: the panel is a fact, not a drawing, and the band's left caption ('FIG. 10 · The core, installed') named the logo's core square, which is retired as illustration. The note's label is 'At the readout', so the AuditSpec line's 'we scope it there' points at the readout call, as it does on /audit. Its place in the band now holds the path line, 'Three questions → a 30-minute call with the founding team → Day 01.' (from QualifyFlow; Mona 15px, paper, drawn arrows). 'Phase 01 / 04 · Diagnose' stays at right. The label row has no meta. Geometry (Swiss skin, 1440 stage), as round 1 A: 948px tall, with 112px top padding. The label row, the 120px statement (line-height .94) and the 48×2 paper rule are 36px apart. The row starts 36px below the rule: panel in cols 1–3 (310×280, A's size, no longer tied to the logo's proportions); lede and doors in cols 5–9 (col 4 left empty as a channel); note in cols 10–12. The band is 104px below, 88px tall, under a margin-to-margin hairline. Alignments: the lede's cap line sits on the panel's top edge. The button's bottom edge is the panel's bottom edge. 'Kickoff · Readout', the button label, the contact link and the note's last line share one baseline (y 727.6, in both skins). Panel: the red surface's --panel (#8E2824 Swiss, #A8302C Kelwin), 24px padding. The 10 is 168px wide-cut 430 in --soft (blush; sand in the Kelwin skin), with proportional figures because Mona's tabular zero is slashed. The unit is 12px mono caps at .12em in paper. The foot is one --line-2 hairline with ten paper ticks hanging from it (01 and 10 at 9px, the eight between at 5px, on a 29px pitch so every tick is crisp), with 14px 'Kickoff' and 'Readout' beneath. Button and link are the kit's .ac-btn and .ac-link, unchanged: the same primary as the hero, which on the red surface is paper fill with red text. Legibility on red: 86%-paper is only 4.2:1 on #BF3A36, which is under the 4.5:1 reading-text minimum for anything below 24px. So every piece of reading type on the plane (label, lede, note, path line, band caption, unit) is full paper at 5.2:1. 86%-paper is kept only for the 120px light statement line, and inside the darker panel, where it is 6.4:1. The blush 10 on the panel is 5.6:1 (sand on the Kelwin panel 3.3:1, a 168px numeral). Nothing is under 11px. Treatments compared: (A) the deep-red panel, kept; (B) a 1px paper hairline frame on the plane with the 10 in paper, rejected because the outlined box read as a ghost button beside the filled one. Red: the plane only. The label squares and the rule invert to paper, and the only red ink is the button's text. ≤760px: one column, 16px gutters, 52px statement; the lede and doors come first, then the panel (max 310px), the note and the stacked band. Checked at 390px with no horizontal scroll. No JS. COHERENCE PASS (round 4): (1) CT2: .copy moved from col 4 / span 6 to col 5 / span 5, opening a channel of plain red between the 10 panel and the action (one column + gutters: 135px from the panel's edge to the button at the 1440 stage); the note gained justify-self: end (flush to the right margin, the band's phase cap shares that edge), so the contact link keeps 87px of air before it (measured on home-u.html with the current kit button). Baselines unchanged. (2) CT1: E6 applied word for word to the lede (now three lines at 40ch). Watch: the note's 'If installation makes sense, we scope it there' now follows the lede's 'If it makes sense, we install it and run it with you' — a deliberate when/what pair (the lede promises, the note says the readout is where it is decided), but if he finds the echo heavy, the note's first clause can drop.
